summary: Edward Joseph Thomas worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a master's at the University of St Andrews under John Burnet (1896–1901) and studied at Cambridge (~1903–1905), later serving at Cambridge University Library and as Dean of Oriental Languages (~1910–1939).

Edward Kamens is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Yale University from ~1970 to 1982 and joined its faculty around 1986, becoming the Sumitomo Professor Emeritus of East Asian Languages & Literatures.

Edward S. Casey is a philosopher who studied at Yale, Northwestern, and the Sorbonne under Paul Ricœur. He taught at UC Santa Barbara, Yale (~1968–1978), and Stony Brook University (~1978), later serving as American Philosophical Association president (2009–2010).

Linguist Edward Sapir studied at Columbia University (~1901–1909) under Franz Boas and Wilhelm Wundt. He served as Chief of Anthropology at the Victoria Museum (~1910–1925) and held professorships at the University of Chicago (~1925–1931) and Yale University (~1931–1939).
Edward Upham worked in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He was a member of the Royal Asiatic Society (~1824–1834) and a fellow of the Society of Antiquaries of London (~1832–1834).

Edward Vernon Arnold specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Cambridge (~1875–1879) and under Rudolf von Roth at the University of Tübingen (~1881–1883), later serving as a fellow at Trinity College, Cambridge, and professor at Bangor University (1884–1924).

Edward W. Said completed studies at Princeton University (~1953–1957) and Harvard University (~1957–1964). He held a long-term academic appointment in English and Comparative Literature at Columbia University from ~1963 to 2003.

Edward Washburn Hopkins studied at Columbia and earned his Ph.D. at Leipzig under Albrecht Weber and Ernst Windisch. A scholar of Indology and linguistics, he taught at Bryn Mawr College (1885–1895) before serving as professor at Yale University (1895–1926).

Edward Winslow Bastian is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied as a research scholar at Banaras Hindu University and earned his Ph.D. from the University of Wisconsin-Madison, supervised by Geshe Lhundup Sopa alongside traditional Tibetan teachers.

Edwin Arnold was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Japanology who studied at King's College London and Oxford. He served as principal of Deccan College (1856), a fellow at the University of Mumbai (~1858), and founded the Maha Bodhi Society.

Edwin Felix Thomas Atkinson worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at Trinity College Dublin (~1857–1861), he served as President of The Asiatic Society (1886–1887) and Accountant General for the Government of Bengal (~1888–1890).

Edwin Francis Bryant is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who earned his doctorate from Columbia University (~1991–1997). He taught at Harvard University (~1997–2003) and became Associate Professor of Hinduism at Rutgers University (~2003).

Edwin Gerow studied Indology and philosophy under J. A. B. van Buitenen, Louis Renou, George V. Bobrinskoy, and V. Ranganathan. He held posts at the University of Washington (~1966–1978) and Reed College (~1978–2001), also editing the Journal of the American Oriental Society.

Edwin Norris was an Indologist, linguist, and historian. After serving as a clerk for the East India Company (1818–1837), he worked as a Foreign Office translator (1847–1866) and held several administrative and librarian roles at the Royal Asiatic Society between 1836 and 1872.

Edwin Whitfield Fay studied at Rhodes College and Johns Hopkins University under Maurice Bloomfield and Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve. A linguist and Indologist, he taught at Washington and Lee University (1893–1899) and the University of Texas at Austin (from 1899).

Egaku Maeda studied Buddhist studies and Indology at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji, Shoson Miyamoto, Hajime Nakamura, and Kogen Mizuno. He held professorships at Tokai Gakuen Junior College, Meijo University, and Aichi Gakuin University (1972–2002).

Eido Shimano was a Buddhist studies figure who trained under Soen Nakagawa and other traditional masters, studying at Ryutaku-ji and the University of Hawaiʻi. He served as abbot at the Zen Studies Society (~1972–2010) and led New York Zendo Shobo-ji and Dai Bosatsu Zendo Kongo-ji.

Eiichi Imoto was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology who studied at Kyoto University (~1949–1953). He held academic posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (~1964–1995) and Momoyama Gakuin University (~1995–2001).

Eiichi Makino was a scholar of philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1899–1903). He served as a professor at the University of Tokyo (~1903–1938) and later held posts at Chuo University (~1938–1946) and Shiraume Gakuen Junior College (~1953–1968).
Eiichi Otani is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at Toyo University from ~1987 to 1991 and held a post as professor and dean at Kyoto Bunkyo University around 2004.
